findings.summary: Brisling has lower median latency (41 ms) than Talmar (118 ms) on the Brindle-Voice test set, but this comparison is confounded by different hardware and precision (Brisling on Corvex A2 fp16 vs Talmar on Corvex A1 fp32).
findings.scope: Brindle-Voice test set, batch size 1, median latency per utterance
findings.caveats: Latency measured on different accelerators and precisions; Talmar latency copied from original paper, not re-measured.

findings.summary: Brisling uses 4.0 decoder passes per utterance versus Talmar's 37.6 passes, indicating a large reduction in decoding steps.
findings.scope: Brindle-Voice test set, decoder passes per utterance
findings.caveats: Passes are averaged over the test set; no statistical test reported.

findings.summary: Brisling's WER (6.4%) is slightly higher than Talmar's (6.1%) on the Brindle-Voice test set, but the difference is small and no statistical test was reported, so it cannot be claimed as significant.
findings.caveats: No statistical test reported; difference may not be reliable.

findings.summary: Brisling has higher WER (6.4%) than Greedy-CTC (8.9%)? Actually, Brisling has lower WER (6.4%) than Greedy-CTC (8.9%), and higher latency (41 ms vs 22 ms).

findings.caveats: No statistical test reported; latency measured on same hardware for both.

drafts.passage: On the Brindle-Voice test set, Brisling achieved a median latency of 41 ms per utterance, substantially lower than Talmar's 118 ms, although this comparison is confounded by the fact that Brisling was measured on a Corvex A2 accelerator in fp16 while Talmar's latency was copied from its original paper, which used the previous-generation Corvex A1 in fp32. Brisling required only 4.0 decoder passes per utterance compared with Talmar's 37.6, reflecting a large reduction in decoding steps. In terms of accuracy, Brisling's WER of 6.4% was slightly higher than Talmar's 6.1%, but no statistical test was reported, so this difference cannot be claimed as significant. Relative to the Greedy-CTC reference, Brisling achieved a lower WER (6.4% vs 8.9%) at the cost of higher median latency (41 ms vs 22 ms), with both measured on the same hardware.
